item.text: The bus the sound plays on; each bus has its own volume and mute under the master ones.
The sound file to play (.wav or .ogg).
An action of this name plays the clip; empty means none.
Plays the clip at the first update of its scene as the active one.
The volume of this source: 0 is silent, 1 is full.
Debug helper: this action gives the quad of the node a random colour; empty reacts to any action.
The action a click on the node emits; empty emits none.
Takes the press, the release and the motion over the shape even with no action, and emits nothing: a shield for what is drawn below.
The clickable area inside the node's rect: the rect itself, or the ellipse inscribed in it.
An action of this name fires a burst of the effect's burst count at the centre of the node; empty means none.
The particle effect as data: how many particles, where they are born, how they move and look.
Starts the effect when the component is attached; a one-shot effect then fires at the first update.
How the quad blends with what is behind it; Alpha is straight alpha. A renderer may ignore it and draw with Alpha.
The fill colour of the node's rect, alpha included.
SceneView only: the document covers the whole output, so it also lays out the bars around the view.
Whether a shown document takes mouse input.
ScaleWithScreen only: 0 follows the width of the output, 1 its height, a value between them blends the two.
The highest scale of a Screen canvas; 0 or less sets no limit.
The lowest scale of a Screen canvas; 0 or less sets no limit.
While shown, no mouse event gets past this document.
The height the screen was designed for, in UI units; ScaleWithScreen scales against it.
The width the screen was designed for, in UI units; ScaleWithScreen scales against it.

How a Screen canvas gets its scale: a UI unit is a window unit (ConstantPixelSize), the same times the user's display scale (ConstantPhysicalSize), or the output size against the reference size (ScaleWithScreen).
The .rml document to load; empty means the markup is set by code.
What the document fills: the whole output (Screen), the fitted view of the scene (SceneView) or the node's box (World).
Lays the content out inside the safe area of the display (Screen and SceneView only).
Whether the document is drawn and, with input enabled, takes input.
How the sprite blends with what is behind it; Alpha is straight alpha. A renderer may ignore it and draw with Alpha.
Stretch covers the whole rect of the node; Contain keeps the aspect of the source and centres the picture in the rect.
Mirrors the picture left to right about its own centre.
Mirrors the picture top to bottom about its own centre.
A sprite of the Sprite Library. While it names one, the library gives the texture and the source rect.
The part of the texture that is drawn, in texture pixels; an empty rect draws the whole texture.
The image file to draw, used when no sprite of the library is chosen.
Where each line stands horizontally in the node's rect.
The colour of the glyphs, alpha included.
A family of the families table of TextConfig.xml; empty is its default family. A font path wins over it.
A font file; empty uses the face of the family and the weight.
The size of the font in scene units.
The CSS weight (400 regular, 700 bold); the nearest face of the family is used.
A factor of the line height of the font.
The smallest size AutoFit shrinks the font to, in scene units.
The colour of the outline; a transparent one draws none.
The width of the outline in scene units; 0 draws none.
What happens to text that does not fit the rect: Clip cuts it, Ellipsis ends it with an ellipsis, AutoFit shrinks the font down to the minimum size.
The colour of the hard shadow; a transparent one draws none.
How far the shadow is to the right of the text, in scene units; two zero offsets draw no shadow.
How far the shadow is below the text, in scene units; two zero offsets draw no shadow.
The text drawn in the node's rect.
Breaks a long line at the width of the rect.
The height of the node's rect, in scene units.
The horizontal place of the rotation pivot in the node's rect: 0 is the left edge, 1 the right edge.
The vertical place of the rotation pivot in the node's rect: 0 is the top edge, 1 the bottom edge.
Turns the node's quad or sprite about the pivot, in degrees, clockwise on the screen. Text, UI and hit tests ignore it.
The width of the node's rect, in scene units.
The left edge of the node's rect, in scene units.
The top edge of the node's rect, in scene units; y grows downwards.
The elements written in the scene file. They are saved with the scene and drawn after those of the source file.
SceneView only: the canvas covers the whole output, so it also reaches the bars around the view.
Whether a shown canvas takes mouse input.
ScaleWithScreen only: 0 follows the width of the output, 1 its height, a value between them blends the two.
The highest scale of a Screen canvas; 0 or less sets no limit.
The lowest scale of a Screen canvas; 0 or less sets no limit.
While shown, no mouse event gets past this canvas.
The alpha factor, 0 to 1, the tree and the popups are drawn with; paint only, and the tooltip is not faded.
The height the screen was designed for, in UI units; ScaleWithScreen scales against it.
The width the screen was designed for, in UI units; ScaleWithScreen scales against it.

How a Screen canvas gets its scale: a UI unit is a window unit (ConstantPixelSize), the same times the user's display scale (ConstantPhysicalSize), or the output size against the reference size (ScaleWithScreen).
A screen in a file of its own (.ui.xml); its elements come first, those of the scene after them.
What the canvas fills: the whole output (Screen), the fitted view of the scene (SceneView) or the node's box (World).
The seconds a show of the canvas takes; 0 or less shows it at once.
The easing curve of the show and hide transition.
Fades the canvas during a transition.
The seconds a hide takes; a negative value uses the duration of the show.
Whether the canvas takes input while it is showing or hiding.
The scale of the hidden end of the transition, about the centre of the canvas; 1 does not scale.
How far to the right the hidden end of the transition is moved, in canvas units; 0 does not slide.
How far down the hidden end of the transition is moved, in canvas units; 0 does not slide.
Lays the content out inside the safe area of the display (Screen and SceneView only).
Responsive variants: overrides of elements that apply while their condition holds for the size of the canvas.
Whether the canvas is drawn and, with input enabled, takes input. A change starts the transition.
